title: AI agents on Google Cloud
summary: The Google Cloud agent platform as a paved road: the product map and how to read its status, ADK, running and deploying agents, agent identity, gateway and registry, regulated-environment controls, then observability, retrieval, memory and a platform design capstone.
intro: This module teaches the Google Cloud side of building and operating AI agents. It starts with the map: which products exist today, what they used to be called, and how to read a Preview or GA label with its date. It then builds an agent with the Agent Development Kit, runs and deploys it, and adds the controls an operated agent needs: its own identity, a gateway that decides what it may call, a registry of agents and tools, and the network and key controls of a regulated environment. Later lessons cover observability and evaluation, retrieval and grounding, agent state, and a design capstone for an internal agent platform. The vendor-neutral ideas (agent patterns, MCP, RAG, identity, observability) are taught in other modules and linked, not repeated.

lessons.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: the map, the names and how to read its status
Where an agent runs: Agent Runtime, Cloud Run and GKE
Identity, gateway and registry for agents (with MCP and A2A on Google Cloud)
Running agents in a regulated environment: VPC Service Controls, CMEK, residency, access controls
Observability, evals and cost for agents on Google Cloud
Grounding and retrieval on Google Cloud: RAG Engine, Vector Search, BigQuery, AlloyDB
Agent state: Sessions, Memory Bank and Code Execution
A paved road for agent teams on Google Cloud (capstone design)
